title:
Short of funds?
*Your home can help*

lines.say: You own a condo worth two point nine million dollars. You see a good investment opportunity, but you don't have the funds.
lines.cap: you see a good investment. *but no funds*

lines.say: Your home could help. You can refinance, and unlock some of its value as cash.
lines.cap: refinance and *unlock some of its value*

lines.say: Banks usually let you borrow up to about 75% of its valuation in total.
lines.cap: banks usually cap total borrowing at *~75% of valuation*

lines.say: But it's not all cash in hand. They subtract your existing loan, plus the CPF you used and its accrued interest.
lines.cap: minus your *existing loan* and *CPF used + interest*

lines.say: Say you owe eight hundred thousand, and used three hundred thousand of CPF. 75% of two point nine million is two point one seven five million. Take away both, and you could unlock about one point zero seven million.
Your income still has to pass TDSR. Repayments on all your loans must stay within 55% of your income.
lines.cap: your income still has to pass *TDSR 55%*

lines.say: We've found it works when the new investment is likely to grow faster than the loan costs. If not, you're just adding debt to your home.
lines.cap: works when growth beats *the loan cost*. if not, it's just debt

lines.say: Want to see how much your property could unlock? Comment unlock.
lines.cap: how much could you unlock? comment *UNLOCK*

source: Bank equity loan guidelines · example figures
caption:
You own a $2.9M condo and see a good investment, but you don't have the funds. 🔑

You could refinance and unlock cash. Banks usually cap total borrowing at about 75% of valuation, minus your existing loan and CPF used plus interest. Example: owe $800K, used $300K CPF, unlock about $1.07M. TDSR still applies.

Want to see how much your property could unlock? Comment UNLOCK 👇

Example figures only. Bank policies vary.
